briefing.body: Following the September 23 sync with Dr. Skinner, the team shifted focus to Preliminary Design Review requirements, targeting early to mid November. Current priorities are the compute platform decision (TI radar module confirmed, board still under evaluation), the physical build approach, and field data reporting without WiFi, where LoRa is the leading candidate under active range testing. Hardware progress is prioritized over further dashboard work per Dr. Skinner's guidance. All tasks are tracked on the Jira Kanban board.
briefing.author: Joshua Zachariah

decisions.decision: Hera Beacon is handheld, not throwable
decisions.reason: The team's POC direction, an individual display on the device itself, confirmed handheld as the working design. Reasoning: physical rescue always requires a responder to eventually approach the survivor directly, so an operator carried device does not introduce a fundamentally new category of risk beyond what rescue already requires. Open item for testing: detection range and signal penetration through debris draw on the same power budget, so whether the device's realistic standoff distance provides a meaningful safety margin over close range needs empirical validation, this is part of the RF and rebar characterization already planned.

decisions.decision: POC dashboard runs locally, not through AWS
decisions.reason: Standing up real AWS infrastructure, device certificates, IAM permissions, an actual cloud connected dashboard, is genuine additional engineering work that does not serve what the POC is actually meant to prove, that the sensors and display pipeline work. A local dashboard the ESP32 serves on its own WiFi network proves the same core capability and is faster to build, which matters given the deadline. AWS remains the settled choice for the real fleet system later, once multiple deployed pods actually need centralized data aggregation.

decisions.decision: Use AWS as the cloud provider for Hera
decisions.reason: Google discontinued its equivalent service, Cloud IoT Core, back in 2023, so AWS is the only one of the two that still has a real, purpose built product for connecting and managing sensor devices at all.

decisions.decision: How do we get data off an ESP32 in remote locations where WiFi is unavailable and cellular is limited?
decisions.reason: Open. Need a connectivity and offload plan for field deployments with weak or no network.
